newsitem.title: EGYPT: UNHCR welcomes Libya move on stranded Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR welcomes Libya move on stranded Palestinians.

text.p: The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) on Wednesday welcomed Libya's decision to allow the return of Palestinian refugees who have been stranded for more than a year on the border with Egypt.

Some 270 Palestinians have been stuck at the makeshift desert camp in what relief workers have described as appalling conditions since Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi expelled them in September 1995 in a bid to show the futility of the PLO-Israeli peace deal.
Libya reversed that policy on Tuesday, saying it was not possible for the Palestinians to return home.
"We welcome Libya's decision as long as it is for the benefit of the Palestinians and puts an end to their suffering but we are against any forced return," said a spokeswoman at UNHCR Cairo office.
She said a mission relief team had arrived at the camp on Wednesday with $10,000 worth of aid, including canned food, oil and sugar.
There were not any signs of movement yet from the camp, she added.
The Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) also welcomed Libya's decision.

"We appreciate this positive step by the People's Committees and the Libyan leadership asking these people to return to Libya and resume their activities," a spokesman for the Palestinian embassy in Tripoli told Reuters.
He said 270 were still stuck on the border and he could not confirm that they had started moving back into Libya.
Libya said its expulsion of Palestinians was aimed at underlining Israel's control over access to Palestinian territories despite its peace accord on self-rule for the PLO.

Most Palestinians forced from Libya went to countries beyond Egypt but Egypt refused to admit those who had no proof they could continue to another country and they were left stranded at the border in miserable conditions.
